number.why: The served OR 1.96 (1.31-2.93) is printed, but it is an odds ratio and the outcome declares RR. Arm counts and randomised denominators (392/393) are printed. The proposed RR = (76/392)/(43/393) = 0.1939/0.1094 = 1.772 is arithmetically right; my Wald 95% CI from the same counts is 1.25-2.51. Rejecting the OR and using counts is correct.

quotes.span: The prednisone group had a higher incidence of in-hospital hyperglycaemia needing insulin treatment (76 [19%] vs 43 [11%]; OR 1·96, 95% CI 1·31-2·93, p=0·0010).
785 patients were randomly assigned to either the prednisone group (n=392) or the placebo group (n=393)

entry.why: Adults aged 18 or older, hospitalised with community-acquired pneumonia, randomised to prednisone vs placebo, as the question requires.

quotes.span: we recruited patients aged 18 years or older with community-acquired pneumonia from seven tertiary care hospitals in Switzerland within 24 h of presentation
Patients 18 years of age or older admitted for hospitalization from the community or a nursing home with CAP.

missed: The endpoint is hyperglycaemia needing insulin, narrower than 'Hyperglycaemia'. The ruling notes this. The denominators are assumed to be the randomised arms because no analysed set is stated for this outcome. The same pattern (a non-RR ratio served on an RR-declared outcome with counts available) is confirmed, not rejected, in M-03 and M-04. The lane should apply one rule to all of them.
